sentence: A cholesterol test reports total, HDL and non-HDL cholesterol plus triglycerides, and doctors read them with other risk factors.
note: NHS: standard test reports total, HDL, non-HDL; triglycerides measured alongside

sentence: A lipid profile measures lipids in the blood, such as cholesterol and triglycerides.
note: LTO: measures levels of specific lipids such as cholesterol and triglycerides

sentence: The sample is taken from a vein in the arm, sometimes after fasting.
A standard test reports total cholesterol, HDL cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol, and triglycerides are usually measured alongside them.
LDL cholesterol is tested less routinely, and doctors order it when the healthcare team thinks treatment may be needed.
HDL is generally treated as the protective part of the total, and a low HDL counts as a risk marker.
note: blended search summary (LTO lipid page and a PMC article); second pass to confirm

sentence: Non-HDL cholesterol is total cholesterol minus HDL.
It adds up the harmful types of cholesterol, so it can be more informative than LDL alone.
note: LTO: includes more than LDL, can be more informative

sentence: Lab Tests Online UK notes that non-HDL does not need a fasting sample, which makes it practical.
note: LTO: non-HDL does not require fasting

sentence: Triglycerides are a type of fat in the blood.
Fasting is needed only for some triglyceride tests, because fasting triglycerides are more accurate and are done if the non-fasting result is high.
The NHS lists target levels for healthy adults and stricter goals after a heart attack or stroke.
Sources differ slightly on where they place the line for triglycerides, and laboratories differ in their reference ranges.
note: BHF and HEART UK give different non-fasting limits

sentence: For that reason the laboratory report shows the range used for each result.
note: author wording of the same point

sentence: Doctors use the cholesterol result with age, blood pressure and health conditions to estimate the risk of cardiovascular disease.
The QRISK tool estimates cardiovascular risk and helps decide whether treatment is needed.
note: Notts pathway: QRISK can be used to help decide if treatment is required

sentence: For people who already have cardiovascular disease, the pathways skip QRISK because their risk is already high.
note: pathway: for people at high risk QRISK3 not needed; second pass to confirm

sentence: A GP or practice nurse takes the sample, and a finger-prick test may be offered in some pharmacies or at an NHS Health Check in England.
NHS pathways encourage a diet rich in fruit, vegetables and wholegrains and low in saturated fat.
They also encourage regular moderate aerobic activity.
In primary prevention, lifestyle support is given for a few months before the level is reassessed.
note: pathway: 3-6 months of lifestyle optimisation, then evaluation

sentence: Where treatment is needed, the pathways favour a high-intensity statin.
Ezetimibe is a second-line option if the aim is not reached.
Someone who has side effects on a high-intensity statin can be offered a lower dose or another statin.
The test is repeated after treatment starts to see whether the level has fallen.
note: pathway: repeat test about 3 months after starting

sentence: The BHF explains that cholesterol builds up in the artery walls as fatty material called atheroma.
That gradual build-up raises the risk of heart attack and stroke.
Risk rises further in people who also have high blood pressure, diabetes or who smoke.
Most people with high cholesterol have no symptoms.
Familial hypercholesterolaemia is an inherited form of high cholesterol.
South West London guidance describes the risk of heart attack or stroke at a younger age as especially high in this condition.
The BHF lists a high result on a routine blood test, or a heart attack or stroke at a younger age, as warning signs.
NHS guidance says statins may be offered to people at higher risk of cardiovascular disease when healthy lifestyle changes have not helped or are unlikely to help on their own.
They are also used in people who already have heart disease and in people with inherited high cholesterol.
If statins are unsuitable, other cholesterol-lowering medicines can be offered.
The BHF says people usually combine healthy lifestyle choices with medicine to lower cholesterol.
Essex integrated care board guidance lists a better diet, regular activity and a healthy weight as the basics.
A standard cholesterol test reports total cholesterol, HDL cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol, and triglycerides are usually measured with them.
Non-HDL cholesterol is total cholesterol minus HDL, and it covers all the harmful types together.
note: LTO: non-HDL is total minus HDL; includes more than LDL

sentence: Doctors use cholesterol results with age, blood pressure and health conditions to estimate the risk of cardiovascular disease.
note: NHS: GP uses cholesterol with other factors to estimate risk

sentence: Where treatment is needed, guidance recommends lifestyle support and often a statin, with the test repeated afterwards.
